title: Hiring grid by employment type
prompt: Recruiting plans hires for every department and every kind of contract the company uses. Write `solve(departments, employees)` so it returns one row for each department and each employment type.
rules: The employment types are the values of `employment_type` found in `employees`, each counted once however many people have it. It is never missing.
Every department gets every type, even a type nobody in that department has yet, and even a department with no employees.
Return only `department_id`, `department_name` and `employment_type`, in that order.
hints: Two steps: get the list of types, then pair it with every department.
`crossJoin` pairs every department with every type. A join on `department_id` would only give each department the types it already has.
explanation: Get each type once with `employees.select("employment_type").distinct()`, then pair it with every department: `departments.select("department_id", "department_name").crossJoin(types)`. The result has departments × types rows. Without `distinct`, every employee would add a copy of their type and the grid would repeat rows. Joining on `department_id` looks tempting but answers a different question: which types each department already has, so a department with no part-time staff would get no part-time row, and a department with no employees no rows at all.
